entries.text.qc01.asset.bg.core_floor: The night-shift Core Floor, with an inspection bench, instrumented test racks, and a safely opened server chassis.
entries.text.qc01.asset.bg.gate: The Validation Gate audit area, with a traveler station and distinct hold and release tags.
entries.text.qc01.asset.bg.knowledge: The Knowledge Systems desk, where attributable Worklog histories appear on a restrained timeline display.
entries.text.qc01.asset.bg.trace: A Trace analysis bench lit by a task lamp, with instruments and a hand-drawn fault tree.
entries.text.qc01.asset.character.hana.relief: Hana Park stands with the traveler tablet and a quietly relieved expression.
entries.text.qc01.asset.character.hana.skeptical: Hana Park holds a traveler at the Validation Gate with a skeptical, exact expression.
entries.text.qc01.asset.character.jonah.defensiv: Jonah Reed holds the closed Worklog tablet in a guarded, attentive stance.
entries.text.qc01.asset.character.jonah.thoughtf: Jonah Reed pauses thoughtfully with a closed Worklog tablet.
entries.text.qc01.asset.character.malik.defensiv: Malik Okoye holds the Rigline test cable in a guarded stance.
entries.text.qc01.asset.character.malik.focused: Malik Okoye holds a coiled Rigline test cable with focused attention.
entries.text.qc01.asset.character.sora.approving: Sora Chen offers restrained approval, one hand extended and a closed notebook at her side.
entries.text.qc01.asset.character.sora.focused: Sora Chen stands ready to question an assumption, one hand raised and a closed notebook at her side.

entries.text.qc02.s07.abandon.01: This Match returned ABANDONED. This handoff adds no diagnosis, action, or closure beyond that bounded result.
entries.text.qc02.s07.abandon.02: For any fresh attempt, treat its observation window as new work and name what changed versus what stayed fixed.
entries.text.qc02.s07.choice.initial.comparison: Lead with the controlled part and population comparisons.
entries.text.qc02.s07.choice.initial.location: Lead with the fixed location and population context.
entries.text.qc02.s07.choice.initial.prompt: Which evidence should lead the handoff?
entries.text.qc02.s07.entry.01: Night shift leaves Trace quiet enough to hear the four-socket server restart, stop during its startup self-check, and return to silence.
entries.text.qc02.s07.entry.02: POST is the machine’s power-on self-test. This one completes it with two processors, but not with the full four. That difference opens a question; it does not condemn a processor.
entries.text.qc02.s07.entry.03: A processor can move. A socket cannot. The processors have worked in other supported pairings, so keep part identity separate from the fixed location and the board path around it.
entries.text.qc02.s07.entry.04: The live Candidates still include processor seating, memory, the socket path, and the wider board. We need Evidence that makes one location behave differently under a controlled comparison.
entries.text.qc02.s07.follow.01: The next unit also asks whether a replaceable part failed or whether the shared path around it did. This time the path carries redundant power.
entries.text.qc02.s07.frame.comparison.01: Lead with the controlled comparisons. I like a tidy table—monthly puzzle night has consequences—but name the fixed location it leaves behind.
entries.text.qc02.s07.frame.location.01: Lead with where the failure follows the configuration. Then attach every comparison that keeps known-good parts from inheriting the blame.
entries.text.qc02.s07.match.01: The Ticket owns the diagnosis. Use the deck to Observe, test competing Hypotheses, and Isolate an actionable fault before any Repair.
entries.text.qc02.s07.success.01: This Match returned COMPLETED. That status belongs to this Ticket and does not decide why another machine behaves differently.
entries.text.qc02.s07.success.02: For the next Ticket, record what moved, what stayed fixed, and which conditions surrounded each new comparison.
entries.text.qc02.s08.abandon.01: This Match returned ABANDONED. This handoff adds no tested configuration, isolated part, or closure beyond that bounded result.
entries.text.qc02.s08.abandon.02: A fresh attempt must earn its own distinction between the report, its location, and any shared context.
entries.text.qc02.s08.ack.initial.comparison.01: You led the first brief with controlled comparisons. This handoff kept those conditions visible while naming the fixed location beside them; presentation order changed no Match authority.
entries.text.qc02.s08.ack.initial.location.01: You led the first brief with the fixed location. This handoff kept that location visible while adding the controlled comparisons beside it; presentation order changed no Match authority.
entries.text.qc02.s08.entry.01: A redundant-power server starts for a moment, reports voltage outside its allowed range, and shuts down before useful work can begin.
entries.text.qc02.s08.entry.02: Two power supplies sit in separate bays, but their paths eventually meet inside the chassis. Useful Evidence must distinguish a removable part, one location, and something shared downstream without assuming which safe comparison will do it.
entries.text.qc02.s08.entry.03: The alert names a measured voltage condition. It does not name the failed part. If the record turns the alert label into a diagnosis, Gate cannot tell what was actually ruled out.
entries.text.qc02.s08.entry.04: The minimum configuration still fails, and the live Candidates include supply, seating or input, distribution path, and system board. Preserve every arrangement and result.
entries.text.qc02.s08.follow.01: The next warning arrives before the service disappears. Acting early still requires an accountable fault, a protected repair, and proof that recovery finished.
entries.text.qc02.s08.match.01: Locate the fault through Match Evidence. A familiar warning earns no shortcut through Isolate.
entries.text.qc02.s08.success.01: This Match returned COMPLETED. Gate accepts that status for this Ticket without extending its explanation to another case.
entries.text.qc02.s08.success.02: For the next Ticket, keep what was reported separate from the explanation being proposed, and require new Evidence before choosing between local and shared context.
entries.text.qc02.s09.abandon.01: This Match returned ABANDONED. This handoff adds no action, accepted state, or closure beyond that bounded result.
entries.text.qc02.s09.abandon.02: On a fresh attempt, protect what the Ticket says is at risk and decide separately what would count as acceptance.
entries.text.qc02.s09.entry.01: One member of a mirrored storage array remains online while its bay alternates amber and green and management reports predictive failure.
entries.text.qc02.s09.entry.02: A mirrored array keeps equivalent data on more than one member so one path can fail without immediate service loss. Predictive means the controller sees risk before the member is fully offline; it is not a completed outage.
entries.text.qc02.s09.entry.03: Early action is responsible only if member identity, current data protection, change authorization, and an independently checked array state remain explicit. “Action taken” is not an acceptance test.
entries.text.qc02.s09.entry.04: The warning, bay indicator, and controller member record point to the same location. The Match must still distinguish predictive media risk from a member that has already failed.
entries.text.qc02.s09.follow.01: Now we have the opposite problem: the hardware looks healthy while a management warning refuses to leave. Current state and recorded history have to be compared before either is trusted as the complete account.
entries.text.qc02.s09.match.01: Protect the data first. Then let current Evidence support Isolate, Repair, independent Verify, and Documentation in that order.
entries.text.qc02.s09.success.01: This Match returned COMPLETED. That status is scoped to this Ticket and does not dictate the same diagnosis or response for another one.
entries.text.qc02.s09.success.02: I keep old transit maps because routes stay legible when their stops remain distinct. On the next warning, keep intervention and acceptance as separate stops.
entries.text.qc02.s10.abandon.01: This Match returned ABANDONED. This scene adds no explanation, change, or closure beyond that bounded result.
entries.text.qc02.s10.abandon.02: A fresh review should preserve source, target, condition, output, and time before any state changes.
entries.text.qc02.s10.choice.change.current: Lead with current device and enclosure state.
entries.text.qc02.s10.choice.change.history: Lead with the change and alert chronology.
entries.text.qc02.s10.choice.change.prompt: Which evidence should lead the comparison?
entries.text.qc02.s10.entry.01: The management console still marks the storage backplane degraded. Current drive inventory and physical indicators show no matching present failure.
entries.text.qc02.s10.entry.02: A management alert is a recorded state, not the hardware itself. It may describe a live condition, an earlier event, or state that was never refreshed after the machine changed.
entries.text.qc02.s10.entry.03: At the community orchestra, I reconcile the ledger after the event, not instead of it. Here, changing management state first would alter the record we need to judge. Preserve current chronology and device state before any action rewrites that surface.
entries.text.qc02.s10.entry.04: The live Candidates are a current backplane-path problem and obsolete management state. Search can organize what exists; it cannot recover state we erase before comparison.
entries.text.qc02.s10.follow.01: The next record pairs a management-firmware change with a network link that repeatedly drops and returns. The chronology is suspicious; it still needs corroboration before it can support cause.
entries.text.qc02.s10.frame.current.01: Lead with what the machine shows now, then place the alert chronology beside it. Current does not mean complete; it gives the comparison a time anchor.
entries.text.qc02.s10.frame.history.01: Lead with what changed and when, then attach the current inventory. Chronology is a map of the question, not a verdict about the hardware.
entries.text.qc02.s10.match.01: Preserve before you change. The Match owns whether the comparison supports an Isolation and whether any later clear is justified.
entries.text.qc02.s10.success.01: This Match returned COMPLETED. Gate accepts that status for this Ticket without turning it into a verdict for another case.
entries.text.qc02.s10.success.02: For a later review, preserve the before-state and time before changing any record; a tidy after-state is not a substitute for provenance.
entries.text.qc02.s11.abandon.01: This Match returned ABANDONED. This scene adds no elimination, observation count, or causal claim beyond that result.
entries.text.qc02.s11.abandon.02: A fresh attempt begins a new observation window; prior context may guide it, but cannot count as a test that survived interruption.
entries.text.qc02.s11.ack.change.current.01: You led with current state in the alert review. Here that habit kept the present link behavior visible before the version chronology was compared; it changed framing, not Evidence.
entries.text.qc02.s11.ack.change.history.01: You led with change history in the alert review. Here that habit kept the version chronology visible before current link behavior was compared; it changed framing, not Evidence.
entries.text.qc02.s11.entry.01: Across several systems, a network port begins reporting repeated link-down and link-up events after a management-firmware change.
entries.text.qc02.s11.entry.02: Link is the physical connection state between interfaces. Flapping means it repeatedly drops and returns; each return can look healthy while the repeated transitions remain the symptom.
entries.text.qc02.s11.entry.03: At the public observatory, a cloud arriving after a lens change earns another observation, not a verdict on the lens. Here, cabling and interface hardware have been exchanged without carrying the behavior away, but version compatibility remains only a Candidate.
entries.text.qc02.s11.entry.04: A clean comparison keeps configured state, physical path, observation window, and result named. Chronology alone is not enough; the Match must find safe Evidence that makes one Candidate differ.
entries.text.qc02.s11.follow.01: The final case sharpens the boundary: a recovery-capable layer can yield read-only Evidence, and an image can reach volatile memory without writing flash. The approved transfer-and-write flow belongs to Repair authority; writing firmware is the machine-state change.
entries.text.qc02.s11.match.01: Use the Match to test the Candidates. Neither timing nor healthy replacement hardware can perform Isolate by itself.
entries.text.qc02.s11.success.01: This Match returned COMPLETED. That status is scoped to this Ticket and does not make a sequence into a cause somewhere else.
entries.text.qc02.s11.success.02: For a later correlation, keep prior state, intervening change, observation window, and result together; sequence may open a question, but it cannot settle one.
entries.text.qc02.s12.abandon.01: This Match returned ABANDONED. This scene adds no state finding, action, or successful acceptance beyond that bounded result.
entries.text.qc02.s12.abandon.02: On a fresh attempt, record what is known, what authority is missing, and which acceptance boundary must be met before work can be called complete.
entries.text.qc02.s12.entry.01: A baseboard management controller stopped responding after power was lost during a firmware operation. The rest of the board now waits behind a management path that cannot start normally.
entries.text.qc02.s12.entry.02: The BMC is a management controller on the board. Here its indicator remains lit while the board otherwise does not respond. The team does not yet know whether any controller layer remains reachable.
entries.text.qc02.s12.entry.03: A recoverable firmware state and a broader version-set problem remain different Candidates. Read-only state can gather Evidence; receiving an image does not by itself prove either Candidate. The bounded recovery flow remains Repair authority, and writing firmware is the state change. The Match determines which authorized observation applies.
entries.text.qc02.s12.entry.04: An image-transfer tool is not diagnostic Evidence merely because it is available. Moving an image into volatile memory does not write flash, but it remains inside the authorized recovery flow; no generic command authorizes board-specific firmware work.
entries.text.qc02.s12.entry.05: Before any state-changing procedure: confirm exact platform identity, an authorized and integrity-checked artifact, protected configuration, and a fallback boundary. After any Repair, use a separate Verify against the defined acceptance boundary.
entries.text.qc02.s12.follow.01: Six new Tickets are now either documented closures or honestly bounded gaps. Their Service Points record accepted contributions; they do not decide access to the next lesson, and the points already earned remain unchanged.
entries.text.qc02.s12.follow.02: The cases do not share a hidden technical cause. What they share is the discipline to keep observations, changes, proof, and explanations distinct enough for the next person to trust.
entries.text.qc02.s12.match.01: The Match owns the recovery decision. Observe first, isolate only what the Evidence supports, change state only through the approved Repair, then Verify and Document separately.
entries.text.qc02.s12.success.01: This Match returned COMPLETED. Gate accepts that status for this Ticket without inventing which private steps produced it.
entries.text.qc02.s12.success.02: For a later high-risk Ticket, keep observation, authorized action, and independent acceptance as separate entries; the explanation should survive transfer without becoming an instruction.
